name: schadenfreude
quote: The bigger they are, the harder they fall.
description: Pleasure derived from the misfortune of others who were previously successful, sometimes combined with guilt for feeling that way.
perceptions: That person or group was doing well but is now struggling with something.
Their struggle makes me feel better about my situation.
results: The struggle of others may feel like justice or perhaps it validates your own struggles and makes you feel less inferior for a time.
examples: A famous person goes to jail for securities fraud.
A rock star files for bankruptcy.

guidance.description: Schadenfreude: How to Respond When Bad Things Happen to People You Don't Like

commentaries.quote: Experts hypothesize that misfortune afflicting an envied person can bring pleasure because it makes the advantaged target less enviable, as well as removing the underlying envy.
To see others suffer does one good, to make others suffer even more: this is a hard saying but an ancient, mighty, human, all-too-human principle.
To feel envy is human, to savor schadenfreude is diabolic.
Questions about how and why we enjoy the pain of others – what is acceptable, what is “too far” – have featured in some of the greatest works of philosophy and literature for over 2,000 years.
